paper.title_en: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
paper.abstract_en: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $Δv_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.
